## A request for thirty million kroner

**Sources on this page:** p205 A1, p205 A2, p205 A3, p205 A4.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-p205-a-a-request-for-thirty-million-kroner"></a>


[Source and verification](../experiments/corpus_joint/README.md)

**Record:** p205 A, four parts, intercepted on 17 November 1918 with an internal `1600 (16)` time/date. **Result:** the published Nov16–18 partial key fixes **481 of 486 plaintext positions** from all **972 printed coordinates**. The financial instructions are readable; five characters in the closing references remain unknown.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-p205-a-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Zur Geldanforderung bei OHL: Sendung von dreißig Millionen Kronen angesichts starken Notenmangels nur in Teilbeträgen möglich. Wiener Bankverein, Wien, überweist heute telegraphisch an Oesterr.-Ungarische Bank, Kronstadt, zur Verfügung deutscher Etappenverwaltung zunächst fünf Millionen gemischter Stückelung. Drahtet, ob glatte Auszahlung erfolgte und ob dieser Betrag vorläufig gemügt [genügt]. Sonst anfordert weitere Summe bei General-Kriegskasse, Zweigstelle Berlin. K `?` BD Nr. `1???` Strich 11 `B?`.

**English meaning:** Concerning the request to the Supreme Army Command for money: a shipment of thirty million kroner can only be made in installments because banknotes are in short supply. The Wiener Bankverein in Vienna is transferring an initial five million, in mixed denominations, to the Austro-Hungarian Bank at Kronstadt for the German rear-area administration. The recipient should telegraph whether payment went smoothly and whether the amount is sufficient for the time being; otherwise, further funds should be requested from the General War Treasury's Berlin branch.

Word spacing, punctuation and capitalization are editorial. Three obvious-looking word repairs still require changes to valid printed coordinates: `Z2R → ZUR`, `ETAPPENVWRWALTUNG → ETAPPENVERWALTUNG`, and `BERL2N → BERLIN`. They are kept separate from the raw decipherment. No value is supplied for any of the five unknown closing-reference characters.

The literal A3 spelling is `GEMUEGT`, displayed as **gemügt**. The bracketed
**[genügt]** is a prose-only normalization, not a fourth coordinate repair.
The closing fields display all five unresolved positions explicitly:
one after `K`, three in `1???`, and one in `B?`. Their separator `X`
characters are represented by spacing; none of those unknown positions is
replaced by an ellipsis or a guessed digit.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-p205-a-the-four-parts"></a>

### The four parts

| Part | Printed coordinates | Fixed plaintext positions | Direct result and qualification |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| A1 | 236 | 118/118 | The thirty-million-kroner request and shortage of notes; begins with literal `Z2R`. |
| A2 | 304 | 152/152 | Vienna bank, telegraphic transfer, Kronstadt and German administration; literal `ETAPPENVWRWALTUNG`. |
| A3 | 234 | 117/117 | Initial five million in mixed denominations; asks about payment and sufficiency. No editorial change. |
| A4 | 198 | 94/99 | Further requests to the General War Treasury's Berlin branch; literal `BERL2N` and five unknown reference characters. |

FUENFXMILLIONENXGEMISCHTERXSTUECKELUNGXDRAHTETXOBXGLATTEXAUSZAHLUNGXERFOLGTEXUNDXOBXDIESERXBETRAGXVORLAEUFIGXGEMUEGTX

The proposed word corrections cost one transmitted-coordinate substitution each: A1 index 162 `V → F`; A2 index 77 `A → G`; A4 index 90 `D → A`. Indices restart at zero for each part. All other printed coordinates are retained. The [certificate](../experiments/corpus_joint/p205_readings.json) records every character's domain and its source offsets, including the dependencies imposed by one common injective partial square.

<a id="edition-cases-finance-p205-a-source-assembly-and-credit"></a>

### Source assembly and credit

The four printed parts are reproduced in the [p205 A crop](../experiments/corpus_joint/sources/p205_A.png). The OCR split A1 after its first eight groups and appended a nonexistent extra unknown character to A4. Joining the source's A1 lines and removing that OCR artifact restores the printed geometries of 236 and 198 coordinates; neither operation deletes a printed coordinate. A2's source group 16 is visibly `FXAFF`, replacing an OCR question mark but retaining the printed `A` that causes the `VWRWALTUNG` garble.

The historical source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p205, PDF page 208 in the [complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). Its header is `NKJ v LP`, with `FUER UKS` and `O K M HERMANNSTADT`; these routing details do not change the supplied plaintext.

The period key retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../data/keys.json) to **George Lasry** and the historical/research work of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. Source assembly, review, exact coordinate audit and this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

python3 experiments/corpus_joint/verify_p205.py

## Naval reporting after dissolution of the Seekriegsleitung

**Sources on this page:** p205 B1, p205 B2.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p205-b-naval-reporting-after-dissolution-of-the-seekriegsleitung"></a>


[Source and verification](../experiments/corpus_joint/README.md)

**Record:** p205 B, two parts, intercepted on 17 November 1918 with the internal date `16/11`. **Result:** the unchanged Nov16–18 partial key fixes **269 of 271 plaintext positions** from all **542 printed coordinates**. The order ends submission of the daily reports and war diaries to the dissolved command, while requiring offices to continue keeping their diaries.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p205-b-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Mit Auflösung der Seekriegsleitung fallen die bisher dahin erstatteten Tagesmeldungen fort. Das gleiche gilt für Vorlage der Kriegstagebücher. Kriegstagebücher [s]ind von allen Dienststellen vorläufig weiterzuführen. Gleichlautend Ost-, Nordflotte, BMK. Admiralstab `1?` Op. Eins.

**Display notes:** The readable German uses the explicitly repaired output. The bracketed `[s]` is the one priced source-coordinate repair, not an abbreviation expansion or a completion of the unknown square. The closing `1?` retains exactly one unresolved numeral position; it is not an unspecified-length omission.

**English meaning:** With dissolution of the Naval Warfare Command, the daily reports previously sent there are discontinued. The same applies to submission of the war diaries. Every office is to continue maintaining its war diary for the time being. The closing names further addressees and gives an Admiral Staff reference whose second digit remains unknown.

Punctuation, word spacing and the separation of the compact addressee string are editorial. The repeated `KRIEGSTAGEBUECHER` is meaningful: one sentence concerns submitting the diaries, and the next concerns continuing to maintain them. It is therefore retained. `BMK` is not expanded to a specific office on the strength of this ciphertext alone.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p205-b-direct-reading-and-one-explicit-emendation"></a>

### Direct reading and one explicit emendation

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MITXAUFLOESUNGXDERXSEEKRIEGSLEITUNGXFALLENXDIEXBISHERXDAHINXERSTATTETENXTAGESMELDUNGENXFORTXDASGLEICHEXGILTXFUERXVORLAGEXDERXKRIEGSTAGEBUECHERXKRIEGSTAGEBUECHER
?INDXVONXALLENXDIENSTSTELLENXVORLAEUFIGXWEITERZUFUEHRENXGLEICHLAUTENDXOSTNORDFLOTTEXBMKXADMIRALSTABX1?XOPXEINSX
```

</details>

Part B1's **160/160 positions** are fixed. Part B2 fixes **109/111**. Its initial unknown is the square cell `GD`, whose possible values under the published partial square are `03456789`. Consequently, `SIND` cannot be obtained by completing an unassigned square cell: `S` is already established at `GA`. The proposed initial `S` requires the single source-coordinate change **B2 index 128 `D → A`**. All other 221 B2 coordinates remain unchanged, and the final unknown digit is left unresolved.

This is a readable editorial reconstruction with an exact one-coordinate cost, not a complete unchanged-source decipherment. The [certificate](../experiments/corpus_joint/p205_readings.json) supplies the two raw texts, all plaintext domains and the edit map.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p205-b-source-and-credit"></a>

### Source and credit

The [p205 B image](../experiments/corpus_joint/sources/p205_B.png) contains 320 coordinates in B1 and 222 in B2. The extra internal space in B1's printed `V AAFX` does not remove a coordinate. The B2 groups `GXXAV`, `FGAXA` and `DDXDV` were checked at higher magnification; their letters are preserved in the source transcription even where the result suggests a copying error.

The historical source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed p205, PDF page 208 in the [complete scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The header reads `ASO v LP (6.38 a.m., November 17th)`, `FUER ASO 1655 (16/11) 2 TEILE B M K SEBASTOPOL`.

The **Nov16–18** period key retains the attribution in [data/keys.json](../data/keys.json) to **George Lasry** and the historical/research work of **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**. Source assembly, review, exact edit costs and this edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.
